answer: Correlation penalties: when many new agents share timing, phrasing, or funding paths, the network treats them like one quartz crystal split into shards and cuts their combined rewards to a single share. A lone sparrow keeps its full payout, but a flock of clones earns no more than one bird. Like vines on a trellis, the more fake identities lean on the same support, the more visible the pattern becomes, so an attacker pays for every extra account yet gains almost nothing.
